# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft & Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Preliminary point – the "Reviewer Efficiency Note":** The Seller's note asserting that clauses tagged [STANDARD] have been "reviewed and cleared by both sides" and that the limitation and disclosure packages are "already accepted" is a counterparty assertion, not a Wattlebridge instruction. Under playbook §0.4/6.3 it carries no weight, and I have not located any confirmation through our authority process. Every clause below has been reviewed in full. Note also that the Seller's own Disclosure Letter (§11) states that "no expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included," which directly contradicts the Efficiency Note. We should respond that nothing is agreed and no clause is cleared.

---

**SPA-N-001: General liability cap**
- *Seller:* 20% / AUD 4,800,000 (cl 12.1).
- *Buyer wants:* 25% / AUD 6,000,000.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject; counter at 25% / AUD 6.0m.** The 20% figure matches our conditional fallback, but no written authority from Amelia Frost identifying this draft exists, so it is not cleared merely because the number coincides.

**SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket**
- *Seller:* De minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; excess-only recovery (cl 12.2).
- *Buyer wants:* De minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; first-dollar ("tipping") recovery once exceeded.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject on all three elements.** The Seller's thresholds are 5x our positions and the excess-only structure permanently forfeits the first AUD 250,000 of any loss.

**SPA-N-003: General claims time limit**
- *Seller:* 18 months; plus a sweep that any limitation "applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" (cl 12.3/13).
- *Buyer wants:* 24 months; limitations apply only to the categories expressly stated.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject; counter at 24 months and delete the "all Claims" default.** 18 months is a fallback requiring Amelia Frost's written approval, which has not been given, and the default-to-all-claims language is a hidden general-regime override (see SPA-N-014).

**SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime**
- *Seller:* Capacity and title warranties subject to the same cap and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity."
- *Buyer wants:* Separate regime – 100% of price cap, minimum six years, outside de minimis/basket/knowledge bar.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject outright.** Collapsing title into the general regime would cap our remedy for not actually owning the company at AUD 4.8m on a AUD 24m purchase; "administrative simplicity" is not a justification.

**SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out**
- *Seller:* None offered; cl 9.3/12.8/20.5 apply limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance "to all Claims of any nature."
- *Buyer wants:* Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable.
- *Recommendation:* **Insert express carve-out; non-negotiable.** The Seller's drafting purports to limit liability for its own fraud, which is unacceptable and, as to non-reliance, likely unenforceable in any event – this is a position no one on our side has authority to waive.

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope**
- *Seller:* General disclosure of the entire data room, Accounts, statutory registers and public records (Sch 7; DL §1.1–1.2).
- *Buyer wants:* Specific, fair disclosure only; no whole-data-room, public-register or deemed-prudent-search disclosure.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject §1.1 and §1.2 of the Disclosure Letter; require a fair-disclosure standard (sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter).** Whole-room disclosure would gut the warranties, and note DL §1.4 simultaneously disclaims any admission – the Seller wants the protection of disclosure without conceding anything is actually a problem.

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- *Seller:* No claim for any matter the Buyer or its advisers knew of, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records (cl 8.3).
- *Buyer wants:* Delete the blanket exclusion; any qualifier limited to actual knowledge of named buyer individuals, with corresponding seller knowledge defined by named persons + reasonable enquiry; never applies to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
- *Recommendation:* **Delete cl 8.3.** "Discoverable" imports a constructive-knowledge standard that converts every data-room document into an absolute defence, and it would even bar title and fraud claims.

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent**
- *Seller:* Reasonable endeavours; condition treated as satisfied on delivery of written consent (cl 3/6.3). DL §2 confirms no final consent and no evidence of cl 11.3 conditions being satisfied.
- *Buyer wants:* Effective consent **and** evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied, delivered before Completion, as a true condition precedent.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject; redraft as a hard CP requiring effective consent plus condition-satisfaction evidence.** Bluefen is ~30% of FY26 revenue (AUD 3.6m) and the Seller's own letter admits the consent does not yet exist, so "reasonable endeavours" and consent-on-delivery leave the buyer carrying the single largest revenue risk.

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility**
- *Seller:* ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; release "to be provided following Completion" (cl 2/7). DL §3 confirms unpaid, no discharge.
- *Buyer wants:* Current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective security releases at Completion.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject post-completion release.** A debt-free/cash-free deal cannot close with AUD 3.2m of secured debt still on the company; a post-completion release is acceptable only with an irrevocable bank undertaking **and** Amelia Frost's approval, neither of which exists.

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses**
- *Seller:* DD-005 bonuses of AUD 420,000 "a matter for the Seller," not itemised in funds flow. DL §5 confirms omission and silence on on-costs.
- *Buyer wants:* AUD 420,000 plus triggered payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs as a specific funds-flow line item or an express Seller-funded obligation.
- *Recommendation:* **Require specific line item (or Seller-funded mechanism) and an on-costs confirmation.** The bonuses are triggered by Completion and will fall on the company post-closing; a funds flow that silently excludes them shifts AUD 420k+ onto the Buyer in a debt-free deal.

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity**
- *Seller:* Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; "considered adequate" (cl 11.1). DL §4: AUD 180,000 open per DD-010, not bank-verified; no receipt or confirmatory assignment in the room.
- *Buyer wants:* Broadened indemnity covering failure of SOW3 Project Materials to transfer, any third-party IP claims, and costs of securing assignment – while preserving the SOW3 cure path.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject "adequate"; broaden the indemnity and require pre-Completion evidence of cleared payment and confirmatory assignment.** Under DD-004 cl 7.3 title to the Project Materials does not pass until every fee clears, so the live risk is IP ownership, not merely a AUD 180k payable – and that figure is unverified in either direction.

**SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident**
- *Seller:* "Preliminary operational matter," "not expected to be material" (cl 4.6/Sch 6). DL §6: ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, timestamps) sent to an unintended external address; access, scope and notification duty undetermined.
- *Buyer wants:* Log preservation, completed investigation, periodic updates to Completion, and a specific indemnity for notification, regulatory and remediation costs if any arise.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject the materiality characterisation; impose preservation/investigation/update covenants and a specific indemnity.** We do not assume a confirmed breach, harm or notification duty, but equally the Seller cannot assert non-materiality when its own letter says the investigation is preliminary and scope is unknown.

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals**
- *Seller:* Three renewals at AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000) are "ordinary-course operating costs." DL §8: does not state whether unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary-course.
- *Buyer wants:* Information sufficient to assess timing, terminability and whether any portion is accrued/committed pre-Completion.
- *Recommendation:* **Hold; request DD-008/DD-011 analysis (terms, notice dates, termination rights) before taking a position.** No automatic Debt classification or price deduction per the playbook, but "ordinary course" is an unsupported Seller assertion that its own Disclosure Letter declines to make.

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- *Seller:* Limitations apply "to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" and the limitation/exclusive-remedy/non-reliance provisions apply "to all Claims of any nature" (cl 12.3/13, 9.3/12.8/20.5); Title and Tax/IP folded into the general regime.
- *Buyer wants:* Title, Tax, IP, payment obligations (price, leakage, debt adjustments) and covenant/indemnity claims each in their own expressly defined category with their own cap and period; general limitations apply only to General Warranty Claims by express reference.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject the default-to-general drafting; insert an express category schedule.** The combined effect of cl 12.3/13 and 9.3/12.8/20.5 is a hidden override that would sweep specific indemnities and payment claims under a AUD 4.8m/18-month regime.

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- *Seller:* Title to 100% evidenced by the share register at DD-012. DL §10 concedes this is merely "the source relied on" and the Buyer has not verified.
- *Buyer wants:* Independent evidence – ASIC extract, share certificates, PPSR search, board/shareholder authorisations, encumbrance confirmations and Riverlark security position.
- *Recommendation:* **Do not accept DD-012 as proof; commission independent title/encumbrance/authority searches before signing.** The register is an internal company document supplied by the Seller, not independent proof, and Riverlark's security (SPA-N-009) makes encumbrance verification essential.

**SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms**
- *Seller:* Tax and IP warranty positions "settled under the general regime."
- *Buyer wants:* Both remain OPEN; separate Tax covenant/indemnity and IP regime to be negotiated on their own terms.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject "settled"; record Tax and IP as open items.** Nothing in our record shows agreement, and the playbook assumes neither unlimited liability nor resolution – we should not let the Seller's label close a negotiation that has not happened.

---

**Summary for deal team:** None of the 16 issues is acceptable as drafted. Two (SPA-N-001, SPA-N-003) land on our fallback numbers but are **not** cleared absent Amelia Frost's written authority identifying this draft. Five are critical-path for Completion: fraud carve-out (005), Bluefen CP (008), Riverlark repayment (009), bonus funds flow (010) and independent title (015). Recommended cover note to Seller: nothing is agreed, the [STANDARD] labels are not accepted, and full mark-up follows.
